pr_comments: @bluca Thank you for the review. Addressed the above points. Upgrading the green label.

issue_context.title: networkd: fails to restore IPv6LL address generation
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
`systemd 250 (250.3-2-arch)`

**Used distribution**
Arch Linux 2022.02.01 (installation iso)

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
`Linux archiso 5.16.4-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT Sat, 29 Jan 2022 19:08:13 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
`x86_64`

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
If a network interface has kernel IPv6LL address generation disabled when networkd is started, networkd re-enables address generation but the interface nevers obtains an IPv6LL address, resulting in the interface being stuck in the `configuring` state.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
1. Boot Arch iso
`qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cdrom archlinux-2022.02.01-x86_64.iso -m 4G`

2. Disable IPv6LL

```
# sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.ens3.addr_gen_mode=1
net.ipv6.conf.ens3.addr_gen_mode = 1
```

Note:
```
0: generate address based on EUI64 (default)
1: do no generate a link-local address, use EUI64 for addresses generated from autoconf
```

3. Clear v6 interface addresses
```
# ip link set ens3 down; ip link set ens3 up

# ip address show ens3
2: ens3: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 52:54:00:12:34:56 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    altname enp0s3
    inet 10.0.2.15/24 metric 100 brd 10.0.2.255 scope global dynamic ens3
       valid_lft 86358sec preferred_lft 86358sec

```

4. Restart networkd
```
# systemctl restart systemd-networkd
```

5. Networkd has restored kernel IPv6LL defaults
```
# sysctl net.ipv6.conf.ens3.addr_gen_mode
net.ipv6.conf.ens3.addr_gen_mode = 0
```
... but it's stuck waiting for an address

```
# networkctl status ens3            
● 2: ens3                                                                      >
                     Link File: /usr/lib/systemd/network/99-default.link
                  Network File: /etc/systemd/network/20-ethernet.network
                          Type: ether
                         State: routable (configuring)
                  Online state: online                                         >
             Alternative Names: enp0s3
                          Path: pci-0000:00:03.0
                        Driver: e1000
                        Vendor: Intel Corporation
                         Model: 82540EM Gigabit Ethernet Controller (QEMU Virtu>
              Hardware Address: 52:54:00:12:34:56
                           MTU: 1500 (min: 46, max: 16110)
                         QDisc: fq_codel
  IPv6 Address Generation Mode: eui64
          Queue Length (Tx/Rx): 1/1
              Auto negotiation: yes
                         Speed: 1Gbps
                        Duplex: full
                          Port: tp
                       Address: 10.0.2.15 (DHCP4 via 10.0.2.2)
                       Gateway: 10.0.2.2
                           DNS: 10.0.2.3
```

Note that if you now toggle (!) `addr_gen_mode` manually it _does_ assign an IPv6LL address..

```
# sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.ens3.addr_gen_mode=1
# sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.ens3.addr_gen_mode=0
```

**Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue**

Some interesting bits from systemd-networkd logs:

```
Feb 04 18:27:42 archiso systemd-networkd[931]: ens3: Setting IPv6LL address generation mode
...
Feb 04 18:27:42 archiso systemd-networkd[931]: ens3: IPv6LL address generation mode set.
Feb 04 18:27:42 archiso systemd-networkd[931]: ens3: master interface set.
Feb 04 18:27:42 archiso systemd-networkd[931]: ens3: link_check_ready(): link is not activated.
Feb 04 18:27:42 archiso systemd-networkd[931]: ens3: Bringing link up
Feb 04 18:27:42 archiso systemd-networkd[931]: ens3: link_check_ready(): IPv6LL is not configured yet.
```

Full networkd debug log: [networkd.log](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ius/ce2a016678b351fe9dc7522e2d466fb5/raw/60c0caf93ba023a5bd2aaaddaf40ceb1dd9f54a0/networkd.log)
comments:
I spent some time debugging this and think I've found the problem.

The `addr_gen_mode` sysctl call chain forces a link local address to be generated ([addrconf.c:6370](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.16.7/source/net/ipv6/addrconf.c#L6370)):
```
addrconf_sysctl_addr_gen_mode -> addrconf_dev_config -> addrconf_addr_gen
```

Networkd doesn't use the sysctl, but instead uses the netlink interface (`IFLA_INET6_ADDR_GEN_MODE`). This updates the interface config ([addrconf.c:5886](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.16.7/source/net/ipv6/addrconf.c#L5886)):

But that doesn't call `addrconf_dev_config` in order to generate an address. A netlink capture confirms the link local address is never assigned. The only path to `addrconf_dev_config` apart from the sysctl is in `addrconf_notify`, which seems to be called on `NETDEV_CHANGEMTU` / `NETDEV_UP` / `NETDEV_CHANGE`.

I suppose that means the kernel expects you to use `IFLA_INET6_ADDR_GEN_MODE` only prior to bringing the interface up. So, the solution would be to change the interface state (not sure if that's appropriate) _or_ use the sysctl to force address generation.

----

I submitted a pull request (#22433) which works for the scenario  I encountered this issue in - specifically: [dhcpcd](https://roy.marples.name/projects/dhcpcd/) sets `addr_gen_mode=1` and drops all IPv6 addresses including IPv6LL upon exit if not configured in _persistent_ mode - but leaves the interface up.

review_comments: Is this intended to be AF_UNSPEC instead of AF_INET6?
`AF_UNSPEC` here is correct. Here, `family` may be `AF_BRIDGE` in some message. This intends to avoid such case.
